findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Lambda console, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve the static IAM credentials and use them outside the function's execution role boundary.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed CMK, and no client-side encryption is used. This weakens key access control and auditability for the stored secrets.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which reached end of support and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the language runtime unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network boundary controls, increasing exfiltration surface if the function is compromised.
